Blankenship is Out [mc11] after an 85.5% snap share [mc12] across 6 games [mc13], so the replacement in deep coverage is the weak point. CLE should look for shots there.

CLE has allowed sacks on 10.8% of dropbacks [mc17] and a 21.4% pressure proxy [mc18]. With Maliek Collins Out [mc19] after a 62.1% snap share [mc20] across 8 games [mc21], the interior rotation thins. Plan quick game and hot throws.

Fourth, finishing drives. CLE converts 34.5% of third downs [mc22] over 119 plays [mc23], 28th in the league [mc24], and scores touchdowns on 42.9% of red-zone drives [mc25] over 21 drives [mc26], 31st [mc27]. Houston allows 39.0% third-down conversions [mc28] and 66.7% red-zone touchdowns [mc29] over 21 drives [mc30], 21st in the league [mc31]. Treat these red-zone samples as directional, but CLE's finishing is the most direct edge available.

report.title: Cleveland vs Houston Scouting Report, Week Ten
report.summary: Houston leans on a deep passing game while its ground attack is inefficient, and its defense is middling against the run and on third down. Cleveland's best path is attacking the light box and the deep middle with Blankenship out. Pass protection and red-zone finishing are the main concerns on both sides.
